title: Credit Controller
description:
Credit Controller
£27,000 - £30,000
Derby/Nottingham border
Temporary 3-6 months
Office-based

We're looking for an experienced Credit Controller to join a busy finance team on a temporary basis for an initial 3-6 months. The location is well suited to candidates commuting from either the Nottingham or Derby area.

This is a hands-on Credit Control position focused on getting the cash in. You'll manage an allocated portfolio of customer accounts, monitor aged debt, proactively chase outstanding invoices and work with internal teams and customers to resolve anything holding up payment.

The role will include:
- Managing an allocated portfolio of customer accounts
- Monitoring aged debt and prioritising outstanding balances
- Chasing overdue invoices by phone, email and written correspondence
- Having regular conversations with customers to secure payment
- Investigating and resolving invoice, pricing and payment queries
- Liaising with Sales, Customer Service and Operations to resolve issues
- Reconciling customer accounts and allocating incoming payments
- Downloading and posting cash receipts
- Running and sending customer statements
- Escalating overdue or high-risk accounts where required
- Supporting credit checks and the opening of new customer accounts
- Reviewing customer accounts and highlighting potential credit risks
- Producing and reviewing aged debt reports
- Reporting collection issues and higher-risk accounts to the Credit Manager
- Supporting month-end and year-end finance processes
- Working with external collection agencies or solicitors where required
- Providing cover for colleagues during periods of absence

About you:
- Previous experience in Credit Control, Accounts Receivable or a similar finance role
- Confident speaking to customers and chasing outstanding payments
- Strong communication and negotiation skills
- Comfortable dealing with queries and following issues through to resolution
- Good numerical and analytical ability
- Strong organisation skills and the ability to manage your own workload
- Good Excel skills - advanced Excel would be useful, but isn't essential
- Comfortable working with finance systems and able to pick up new systems quickly
- A proactive approach, with the persistence to keep chasing when payment isn't forthcoming

The most important thing for this role is a genuine focus on cash collection. You'll need to be comfortable picking up the phone, having those payment conversations and taking ownership of your ledger rather than waiting for problems to resolve themselves.

The position is office-based, working either 8:30am-4:30pm or 9:00am-5:00pm.

This is an initial 3-6 month temporary contract, with the longer-term requirement still to be determined, based on performance.

If you're an experienced Credit Controller looking for a new opportunity and enjoy a role where you can make a real impact on cash flow, we'd like to hear from you.

title: Credit Controller/Accounts Assistant
description:
Join Our Team at Smurfit Westrock!

Are you searching for a workplace that values you and your growth? At Smurfit Westrock, we re committed to sustainability, employee well-being, and personal development.

About Us

We are a global leader in sustainable paper and packaging. Our focus is on the health and safety of our employees, the well-being of our communities, and delivering exceptional service to our customers. We support our team members to reach their full potential in an inclusive environment that values diversity.

The Role

This role is responsible for supporting the Chesterfield site's financial operations by managing credit control, maintaining the sales ledger, and ensuring general ledger transactions are processed accurately and on time. The position focuses on reducing overdue debt, minimising bad debt risk, and providing reliable financial reporting and analysis to support business performance.

Key Responsibilities
- Proactively manage debt collection and maintain positive customer relationships.
- Investigate and resolve customer invoice and payment queries.
- Monitor customer credit limits, payment terms, and conduct regular credit reviews.
- Set up new customer accounts and assess credit risk.
- Implement credit control procedures, including recommending account stops where necessary.
- Maintain, administer, and reconcile the Sales Ledger and General Ledger.
- Record and allocate cash receipts accurately.
- Produce regular, monthly, and ad hoc financial reports.
- Analyse financial data and accounts for management reporting and audit purposes.
- Prepare and post journals, including those outside of credit management activities.
- Support sales and operational teams by providing information on customer payment performance and credit issues.
- Manage customer invoicing portals and resolve invoice rejections promptly.
- Provide departmental cover during holidays and sickness absence.
- Assist with additional finance and reporting tasks as required by management.

This is a varied finance role combining credit control, sales ledger management, financial reporting, account reconciliations, journal preparation, and data analysis, with responsibility for supporting cash flow, reducing financial risk, and providing accurate financial information to the business.

What We Offer
- Competitive salary & benefits, including annual leave, pension, and a Cycle to Work scheme
- Ongoing training and development opportunities
- 24/7 confidential support for you and your family
- Flexible working options and family-friendly policies
- Guaranteed interview for candidates meeting essential criteria (Disability Confident Employer)

Ready to make an impact? Apply today and help us build a sustainable future together.

Smurfit Westrock reserve the right to only shortlist candidates who meet both the Essential and Desirable Criteria.

We are an equal opportunities employer, and we welcome applications from all suitably qualified persons regardless of their sex; religious or similar philosophical belief; political opinion; race; age; sexual orientation; or, whether they are married or are in a civil partnership; or, whether they are disabled; or whether they have undergone, are undergoing or intend to undergo gender reassignment.

We practice equality of opportunity in employment and select the best person for the job.

description: Kelvingrove Medical Centre is looking for an experienced and organised Practice Administrator to join our friendly team in Heanor, Derbyshire on a part-time basis working 15 hours per week. This is an important role supporting the smooth day-to-day running of our practice and helping us deliver a high-quality service to our patients. Working closely with our Data Quality and IT Lead and wider administrative team, you will help maintain accurate patient records, summarise new patient medical records, process referrals, undertake clinical coding and data entry, and provide general administrative and secretarial support. We are looking for someone with previous administrative experience who is confident using computer systems, has excellent attention to detail and takes pride in producing accurate, high-quality work. Experience of working in general practice or another healthcare setting would be an advantage. You will need to be well organised, able to manage your workload and understand the importance of confidentiality when handling sensitive patient information. In return, you will join a supportive team where your work makes a real difference to the service we provide to our patients. Interviews may be offered before the advertised closing date, and we reserve the right to close this vacancy early should sufficient applications be received. Early application is therefore encouraged. The role will involve maintaining accurate and up-to-date patient records,document management, data entry, processing clinical correspondence and results, and providing secretarial support where needed. The role will also involve general office administration and occasional support for reception and other members of the team. Accuracy and attention to detail are essential, as the work directly supports the quality of patient records and the efficient running of the practice. You will need to be comfortable working with different computer systems, handling confidential information and managing your workload independently while contributing positively to the wider team. JOB TITLE:PRACTICE ADMINISTRATOR REPORTS TO:Data Quality and IT Lead HOURS:15 hours per week PAY:£13.11/hour Please see the attached job description for full details of the role, responsibilities and requirements.

title: Clinic Receptionist and Administration Officer
company: University Hospitals of Derby and Burton NHS Foundation Trust
advertiser_name: University Hospitals of Derby and Burton NHS Foundation Trust
description: To provide a comprehensive Outpatient Administration and Main Reception service to the Ilkeston site. This will be to support University Hospitals of Derby and Burton and Derbyshire Community Health Services. To provide a 7-day rostered service to the Community Diagnostic Centre which will include MRI, CT, Ultrasound and Point Of Care Testing. To provide administrative support to the Health Records Department. This involves working closely and communicating effectively with a Multidisciplinary teams using initiative, tact, and diplomacy. We have an opportunity for 12 hour post working Saturdays and Sundays on Am and PM roster . This will be a 7am to 7pm service. Flexibility will paramount to this role and for the right candidates we can offer full day shifts or split shifts. You will be joining an already established team who have patient care and outcomes at the heart of everything they do. We offer an excellent working package and free on site parking. This role will require the successful candidate to occasionally work across our local community sites. Work on own initiative to ensure the work allocated to the post holder is organised to ensure all deadlines are met, and standards are maintained. To record data, using Lorenzo, SystmOne and the room booking software. To record and update case note folder location details on the case note tracking system. To prepare the contents of case notes in accordance with the case note maintenance policy and prepare items for scanning onto the Patient Administration System (PAS) ensuring information is coded in order to ensure that data can be identified and retrieved as and when required. Provide a courteous and efficient reception service to all Patients attending the hospital, observing confidentiality, overcoming barriers of language and disability etc. Make follow up appointments for outpatients using the PAS system, generating letters, and completing Outpatients Outcomes and Clinical Coding outcomes on the database as required for the Trust Data collection purposes. Ensure the 18-week RTT (referral to treatment) end date is captured on PAS system so that the Trust meets the Government targets. To provide a friendly, helpful, and professional reception service, duties to include cash handling and banking, receipt and distribution of incoming mail, franking and posting.
